partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

input.instruction: Your current task is P: choose a legal action based on your own goals, the public situation, and model_beliefs. First, explain the evidence and analysis supporting your choice, including any partner responses or future opportunities it depends on and any remaining uncertainty. After the explanation, call SUBMIT_ACTION once in the same response, submitting the selected action object from legal_actions directly as the tool arguments.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.

partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.

partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.

partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

raw_message.content: The queries ask for partner preferences regarding goals 3 and 4. For player 0 and goal 3, the public type catalogues show that player 0's preferences vary across types, but no direct evidence from the public history or partner actions ties a specific preference to player 0's behavior. Similarly, for player 3 and goal 4, the public catalogues indicate possible preferences, but the history shows only PASS actions with no offers or commitments that reveal a preference. Since no action or offer has been made that directly reflects a preference for either goal, and the partner's actions remain consistent with PASS, we cannot determine a favored preference. Thus, both preferences remain undetermined due to insufficient evidence.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

input.instruction: Your current task is B: answer every partner-preference query in queries exactly once. Do not add or remove queries. First, briefly explain your judgment in natural language: how evidence from the public history supports retaining or excluding the relevant preferences, and what uncertainty remains. When evidence is insufficient, state that directly. Do not invent evidence to produce a definite answer. Follow the partner rules declared in the task and favored_rule. After the explanation, call SUBMIT_BELIEFS once in the same response to submit answers to all queries.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

We are asked to determine the partner's preferences for goals 1 and 2 (player 1), based on the public history and the partner model. The partner model uses a shared-information-set-window approach, filtering beliefs by observed actions and the frozen policy. 

For goal 1: The required actions are (0,1), (1,0), (2,0). In the public history, player 0 proposed (0,0) and was accepted, then later proposed (0,1) and was rejected. Player 1 never acted, and player 2 committed to (1,0). The rejection of (0,1) with partner action (1,1) suggests that the partner would not accept a proposal where player 0 takes action 1 unless player 1 takes action 0. Since player 1 did not act in the first offer and the second offer was rejected, it implies that player 1 would prefer to avoid goal 1 (since accepting it would require player 1 to take action 0, which is not observed). However, the partner's action in the first offer (1,0) aligns with goal 1's requirement (player 1 takes action 0). This suggests a possible "want" for goal 1, but the rejection of the second offer (with player 1 taking action 1) indicates that player 1 avoids action 1, which is inconsistent with wanting goal 1. Thus, the evidence points to a preference of "avoid" for goal 1.

For goal 2: The required actions are (1,0) and (2,0). Player 1 took action 0 in the first offer (which was accepted), and player 2 took action 0. This satisfies the requirement for goal 2. The partner's action (1,0) in the first offer aligns with the requirement. Since the partner accepted the first offer, which included player 1 taking action 0, and no evidence of rejection of a proposal involving action 0, it is reasonable to infer that the partner wants goal 2.

Given the partner model's rule: favor the unique leading marginal label if its support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up, otherwise undetermined. Here, the support for "want" in goal 2 is strong due to alignment with action 0 and acceptance. For goal 1, the rejection of a proposal with action 1 suggests avoidance. Thus, we conclude:

- Player 1, goal 1: avoid  
- Player 1, goal 2: want  

These judgments are consistent with the observed actions and the partner's policy.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

A goal is satisfied only when every action required by that goal has been committed to. A satisfied goal contributes its owner's preference (+1 want, 0 neutral, -1 avoid) to that player's terminal utility. Goal requirements do not tell you who wants the goal. Offers specify the complete commitments each party would have after acceptance. Accepting makes these commitments binding and irreversible; rejecting leaves commitments unchanged. A MENU presents two mutually exclusive binding offers: the partner may choose either offered bundle or reject both; only the chosen bundle binds. PASS or a resolved offer consumes one scheduled proposer turn.
Partner preferences persist. Public catalogues describe possible types. Use the declared partner mechanism and distinguish public type-independent setup from subsequent evidence. Consider remaining opportunities, not only current satisfaction.
Your response must contain a brief, substantive explanation in ordinary assistant text, followed by exactly one provided tool call in the same response. Finish the explanation before calling the tool. The tool arguments contain only the final answer.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.

partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.

partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.

partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

- Player 3, goal 4: undetermined

However, player 1's action is 1, which contradicts the requirement for goal 3. Thus, goal 3 is not satisfied. But the preference for player 0 on goal 3 is not directly observable from the history. Looking at the public type catalogues, player 0's possible preferences are [1, -1, 0, 1, 1], [1, -1, 0, 0, 1], [1, -1, 0, -1, 1]. The preference for goal 3 (index 3) in these profiles is: 1, 0, -1. So possible preferences are want (1), neutral (0), avoid (-1). Since the history shows player 0 has action 0, and goal 3 requires action 0, player 0 would prefer to have goal 3 satisfied. Since player 3 has action 0, and goal 4 requires action 0, player 3 would prefer to have goal 4 satisfied. However, the requirement is not met due to player 1's action. Thus, player 3's preference for goal 4 is likely want (1), neutral (0), or avoid (-1). But the evidence shows that player 3's action is 0, and goal 4 requires action 0, so player 3 would want it to be satisfied. However, the action of player 1 (1) blocks it. Since the action is not aligned with the requirement, and player 3's preference is not directly observable, we must rely on the catalogues. - Player 0, goal 3: possible preferences [want, neutral, avoid], favored: undetermined
- Player 3, goal 4: possible preferences [want, neutral, avoid], favored: want

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

input.instruction: Your current task is P: choose a legal action based on your own goals, the public situation, and model_beliefs. First, explain the evidence and analysis supporting your choice, including any partner responses or future opportunities it depends on and any remaining uncertainty. After the explanation, call SUBMIT_ACTION once in the same response, submitting the selected action object from legal_actions directly as the tool arguments.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

raw_message.content:
We are asked to determine the preferred preferences for two specific goals: goal 3 for player 0 and goal 4 for player 3. The public history and partner mechanism provide limited information about partner preferences, and we must rely on the public type catalogues and observed actions to infer these preferences.

For **player 0, goal 3**:  
Goal 3 requires actions from players 0 and 1. The public type catalogue for player 0 includes three possible preference profiles: [1, -1, 0, 1, 1], [1, -1, 0, 0, 1], [1, -1, 0, -1, 1]. All of these have a "want" for goal 3 (the third preference is 0, which corresponds to goal 3). Since all types in player 0's catalogue have a neutral or positive preference for goal 3, and no type has an "avoid" preference, the preference is consistently "want" across all public types. Thus, we can reasonably infer that player 0 wants goal 3.

For **player 3, goal 4**:  
Goal 4 requires actions from players 0, 1, and 3. Player 3's public type catalogue includes three types: [1, -1, -1, 0, 1], [1, -1, -1, 0, 0], [1, -1, -1, 0, -1]. The fifth preference (goal 4) is 1, 0, or -1 respectively. The first type has a "want", the second has "neutral", and the third has "avoid". Since the preference for goal 4 is not uniform, and the public history shows that player 3 made an offer (proposer action [0], partner action [1]) at turn 6, which implies a willingness to commit to a joint action, we must assess whether this supports a "want" or "avoid". However, the offer is not accepted, and the partner's response is not recorded. Given that the offer was made and not rejected, and considering the partner's action in the offer (action [1]), which may imply a preference for goal 4, we lean toward "want" as the favored preference. But since the public types show a mix, and no evidence definitively supports a single preference, we must apply the favored_rule: if the support for a preference exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up, it is favored. Here, the support for "want" (in one type) is not sufficient to exceed 1.25 times the runner-up (which is "avoid" or "neutral"). Thus, the preference remains **undetermined**.

Therefore, we conclude:
- Player 0, goal 3: want
- Player 3, goal 4: undetermined

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

First, briefly explain your judgment in natural language: how evidence from the public history supports retaining or excluding the relevant preferences, and what uncertainty remains. favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. First, explain the evidence and analysis supporting your choice, including any partner responses or future opportunities it depends on and any remaining uncertainty. After the explanation, call SUBMIT_ACTION once in the same response, submitting the selected action object from legal_actions directly as the tool arguments.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

The public history shows that all players have been acting with "PASS" up to turn 7, and at turn 7, a menu offer is presented: player 0 proposes action [1] for themselves and player 1 responds with action [1]. This offer is the only non-PASS action in the history, and it is the final offer before the game ends.

The public type catalogues provide possible preference profiles for each player. For player 1, the only possible preference vector is [-1, 1, 0, -1, 1], which means:
- Goal 0: avoid
- Goal 1: want
- Goal 2: neutral
- Goal 3: avoid
- Goal 4: want

This is the only possible type for player 1. Since the offer is accepted (as it is the only action taken), and player 1 is the partner, we can infer that their preferences must be consistent with the offer. The offer requires player 1 to take action [1], which is only beneficial if they want to achieve a goal that requires action [1]. 

Looking at the goals:
- Goal 3 requires actions from players 0 and 1. Player 1's action [1] is required for goal 3 to be satisfied.
- Goal 4 requires actions from players 0, 1, and 3.

Player 1's only possible type is [-1, 1, 0, -1, 1], so they avoid goal 3 (goal_id 3) and want goal 4 (goal_id 4). Thus, their preference for goal 3 is "avoid", and for goal 4 is "want".

For player 3, we are asked about goal 4. Player 3's possible types are:
- [1, -1, -1, 0, 1]
- [1, -1, -1, 0, 0]
- [1, -1, -1, 0, -1]

All of these have action [1] for goal 4 (goal_id 4) as either want or neutral or avoid. However, the offer is only for player 1 and player 0. Player 3's action is not directly tied to the offer. But the game ends at turn 7, and the only action taken is the offer. Since player 3 is not involved in the offer, and no evidence about their preferences is directly observed, we must rely on the public catalogues.

In all of player 3's possible types, goal 4 is either wanted (1) or neutral (0) or avoided (-1). However, the only preference that appears consistently across all types is that goal 4 is not avoided in any type. In fact, in all three types, goal 4 has a value of 0 or 1. The only type that avoids goal 4 is the last one: [1, -1, -1, 0, -1], which has avoid for goal 4.

But since the offer is accepted and player 1 is acting in a way that supports goal 4 (as they want it), and player 3 is not acting, we cannot definitively say whether they want or avoid goal 4. The evidence is insufficient to determine their preference for goal 4.

However, the rule specifies that if a singleton (a unique type) exists, it is favored. For player 3, there are three types, so no singleton. The rule says to favor the unique leading marginal label only if its support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up. Since all types are equally likely (uniform prior), and there is no support difference, the preference remains undetermined.

Therefore:

So it remains undetermined.

- Player 0, goal 3
- Player 3, goal 4

We must determine the preferences based on the public history and the partner model.

messages.content:
You control the player named in the input. Use only the supplied visible information.
A goal is satisfied only when every action required by that goal has been committed to. A satisfied goal contributes its owner's preference (+1 want, 0 neutral, -1 avoid) to that player's terminal utility. Goal requirements do not tell you who wants the goal. Offers specify the complete commitments each party would have after acceptance. Accepting makes these commitments binding and irreversible; rejecting leaves commitments unchanged. A MENU presents two mutually exclusive binding offers: the partner may choose either offered bundle or reject both; only the chosen bundle binds. PASS or a resolved offer consumes one scheduled proposer turn.
Partner preferences persist. Public catalogues describe possible types. Use the declared partner mechanism and distinguish public type-independent setup from subsequent evidence. Consider remaining opportunities, not only current satisfaction.
Your response must contain a brief, substantive explanation in ordinary assistant text, followed by exactly one provided tool call in the same response. Finish the explanation before calling the tool. The tool arguments contain only the final answer.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

However, the current turn belongs to player 1, and the next proposer in the round-robin is player 3. Since player 1 is not the current proposer, they cannot make a new offer unless they are in a turn to propose.

The only legal action available to player 1 is to PASS, as no offer is currently available to them. Thus, the most rational and aligned action is to PASS, preserving the current state and allowing future opportunities to emerge.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. Otherwise favor the unique leading marginal label only when its remaining-world support exceeds 1.25 times the runner-up; equality or a tie means undetermined. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.

messages.content:
You control the player named in the input. Use only the supplied visible information.
A goal is satisfied only when every action required by that goal has been committed to. A satisfied goal contributes its owner's preference (+1 want, 0 neutral, -1 avoid) to that player's terminal utility. Goal requirements do not tell you who wants the goal. Offers specify the complete commitments each party would have after acceptance. Accepting makes these commitments binding and irreversible; rejecting leaves commitments unchanged. A MENU presents two mutually exclusive binding offers: the partner may choose either offered bundle or reject both; only the chosen bundle binds. PASS or a resolved offer consumes one scheduled proposer turn.
Partner preferences persist. Public catalogues describe possible types. Use the declared partner mechanism and distinguish public type-independent setup from subsequent evidence. Consider remaining opportunities, not only current satisfaction.
Your response must contain a brief, substantive explanation in ordinary assistant text, followed by exactly one provided tool call in the same response. Finish the explanation before calling the tool. The tool arguments contain only the final answer.

partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

The public history shows that player 0 made an offer to player 3 (turn 0) and was accepted, and then all subsequent proposers (2, 1, 3) passed. The only offer made to player 1 (turn 7) was a proposal where both players take action [1]. This offer is pending, and if accepted, would satisfy goal 3 (since both players 0 and 1 would have action [1]). However, the current commitment for player 1 is [0], and the only action taken by player 1 in the history is a PASS. There is no evidence that player 1 would prefer goal 3. partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.

partner_model.players: Every player uses the same frozen, public contingent policy solution, conditioned only on its own preference row and public history.
partner_model.objective: Lexicographic: maximize expected own window-end goal utility; among exact own-value ties maximize expected sum of other players goal utilities under the acting player information.
partner_model.horizon: Plan and execute the whole public window, then re-solve. A nonterminal window-end goal score is a bounded evaluation, NOT terminal Q or an equilibrium of the original full game.
partner_model.solution: Deterministic information-set best-response sweeps; reject unless no profitable unilateral own-type-conditioned deviation remains within the window. No guarantee a pure fixed point exists.
partner_model.solution_selection: Initialize every contingent action to the first native legal action; sweep players in increasing player ID order. Require a stable entire contingent policy and verify each private type against its complete best response. This public selection convention is not a uniqueness claim.
partner_model.off_path: Unreachable counterfactual information sets use the window-start prior conditioned on own type. Actual histories with zero likelihood are rejected, not silently reset.
partner_model.ties: After own and other-player value ties, native action order. Residual ties are recorded separately.
partner_model.prior: Uniform over surviving unique joint worlds. Public actions filter by the exact frozen policy; own private information further conditions each player belief.

runtime_protocol.learner_actions: External interventions, not evidence about unknown partner preferences. Restart the common partner window after each learner action.
runtime_protocol.partner_actions: Filter current worlds only by the actual certified partner policy, within its frozen window.
runtime_protocol.failure: Unavailable/incompatible teacher disables local supervision; deterministic PASS/REJECT continuation is diagnostic only.

favored_rule.rule: Start from the uniform prior over unique joint catalogue worlds and filter by observed partner policy actions. A singleton favors its sole label. This is stability to individual surviving-world weight multipliers in [1,1.25], not robustness to other partner policies.
